timeline.text: Chest x-ray: right lower lobe opacity
Transthoracic echo: LVEF 55%, grade I diastolic dysfunction

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 86-year-old female admitted for community-acquired pneumonia. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.71, bnp 203, creatinine 0.75, hemoglobin 12.8, platelets 254, sodium 140, wbc 8.6; vitals dbp 76-80, heart_rate 85-89, map 90-95, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 13-14, sbp 118-125, spo2 97-98, temp 36.5-36.8
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Chest x-ray: right lower lobe opacity; Furosemide 20 mg PO daily (home med); Transthoracic echo: LVEF 55%, grade I diastolic dysfunction
Assessment and plan: Community-acquired pneumonia. Hypertension.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.76, hemoglobin 12.8, platelets 264, sodium 140, wbc 8.4; vitals dbp 77-80, heart_rate 87-90, map 91-94, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 13-15, sbp 119-123, spo2 97-98, temp 36.5-36.8
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Furosemide 20 mg PO daily (home med)
Assessment and plan: Community-acquired pneumonia. Hypertension. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 86-year-old female, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Community-acquired pneumonia. Hypertension. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
